newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX eyes link with a European exchange this year.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX eyes link with a European exchange this year.

text.p: Singapore's futures exchange hopes to forge a link with a European exchange this year with an eye to trading a contract based on the single European currency, the head of the exchange said on Thursday.

"We have been in discussions and I'm optimistic that some form of conclusion can be reached some time this year," Ang Swee Tian, president of the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) told Reuters.
He said such a link would also help to revive trading interest in the SIMEX Euromark contract.

"The SIMEX Euromark contract is more or less dormant ... So there have been suggestions by our members that in order for this contract to work, we need to forge a link with the primary market in Europe," Ang said.
He said SIMEX had been holding discussions with the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE), the French futures exchange, MATIF and DTB, the German exchange.

The link could take the form of a mutual offset arrangement, similar to the ones SIMEX has established with the Chicago Mercantile Exchange for the trading of U.S. and Japanese interest rate futures contracts, Ang said.

In addition to contracts based on the Euro and short-term European interest rates, Ang said SIMEX was also exploring the possibility of trading contracts based on longer-term contracts such as German bunds.
"We hope to be able to provide a gateway for the European exchange to enable them to reach out to customers in this part of the world," he said.
